subsections.label: Project Aspire — Bina
points: Bina Petrochemical and Refinery expansion achieved 23% progress against planned 32%, with INR4,700 crores incurred and INR25,400 crores committed. Schedule variance primarily due to geopolitical developments and supply chain challenges affecting manufacturing and delivery.

Critical long lead items remain on track; all major packages awarded by February 2026. Recent Middle East conflicts impacted supply pricing and execution timelines; mitigation measures being implemented.

Total project cost ~INR49,800 crores of which only ~INR6,500 crores is foreign component; a 10% depreciation could move it to ~INR6,000-7,000 crores. Around INR25,000 crores tenders awarded on fixed price contract so no price impact on awarded work; 20-25% yet to be awarded. Hopeful of completing within plus/minus 10% of approved cost.

subsections.label: Andhra Pradesh refinery-cum-petrochemical project
points: Proposed 9 MMT per annum refinery and petrochemical complex; key preparatory activities progressing as planned. Environmental and technical studies completed; detailed engineering and financial appraisal underway. Supported by strong incentives from Andhra Pradesh government.

subsections.label: Other major projects
points: PRFCC project at Mumbai refinery, polypropylene project at Kochi, and POL and LOBS installation at Rasayani progressing steadily in line with planned commissioning timelines.
PRFCC at Mumbai approved last year; work just started with licensor selection and BDEP ongoing; no major cost escalation foreseen at this point.

subsections.label: Upstream — Mozambique
points: On 7 November 2025 the operator informed Government of Mozambique that force majeure has been resolved; work resumed in full swing, first LNG cargo expected by mid-2028. ~6,000 manpower at site, ~42% project schedule completed.

Reserve size ~70 TCF; first phase development for 13 TCF, BPCL stake 10%; 42% complete. First phase mostly under project finance with no equity commitment from BPCL; future investments mainly from project financing; subsequent phases funded from first-phase cash flows — no future equity capital commitment from BPCL.

subsections.label: Upstream — Brazil (BM-SEAL-11)
points: FPSO tender finalized and to be awarded shortly; work commissioned for development, first gas expected 2031-32; FID approved by operator.

Total project capex ~$6.4 billion, BPCL share ~40% (~$2.8 billion); future capital contribution ~$1.2 billion over 3-4 years, in one field development with potential for another development (similar size reserves estimated).
Expected daily crude production ~88,000 barrels per day, 40% through JV IBV; equity crude rights can be brought to India or marketed based on commercial position.
Revised cost approved at Board level subject to government approvals.

subsections.label: Upstream — UAE / Urja Bharat
points: Through SPV Urja Bharat Private Limited, first oil discovery in the unconventional Shilaif play made in XN-76 well in UAE; BPRL also witnessed oil discovery during testing of exploration well XN-79 02S in Onshore Block 1.

Lower Zakum and upper Zakum blocks in UAE (India consortium ~10% stake) already producing good volume; new discovery completed in FY26 to move to development plan; hopeful of good extractable reserves.

subsections.label: Capital allocation philosophy
points: To grow beyond the energy sector's 2-3% annualized growth, company diversifies within/beyond the energy sector to optimize returns.

Petrochemical integration with refinery intermediaries gives good value addition; India petrochemical products largely import-driven with 5-7% growth, hence major capital allocation to petrochemicals.
Upstream capital targets 6-7 MMT of own crude (rights or profit share) versus current low own-feed relative to 41 MMT refining capacity.
Comfortable with netback period of 5-6 years such that 80-90% of investment returns in 4-5 years; only allocates capital where commercial returns are clear (cites IREP returns).

subsections.label: Geopolitical / supply disruption
points: Ongoing tension in West Asia driving global and domestic economies through an uncertain phase; major disruption in global energy supply chains across all sectors and geographies.

Crude and product prices, broadly range bound for much of FY25-26, witnessed heightened volatility toward year-end with disruptions to flow through the Strait of Hormuz. Forex fluctuations and geopolitical developments remain key drivers.
Full war impact not realized in Q4 due to timing differences; Q1 FY27 is going to be a challenging period.
Recent Middle East conflicts impacted supply pricing and execution timelines for projects (notably Bina).

subsections.label: Under-recovery / cash-flow stress
points: Severe under-recoveries across products; while technically deregulated, no roadmap for recovery of under-recoveries; LPG remains regulated.

Company can absorb the current environment only for a limited period (1-2 months of cash-flow mismatch); if it continues, no balance sheet can absorb and there will be stress absent price revisions — burden must be shared among stakeholders.
Freight cost sharply increased (world scale from ~50-55 pre-war to 600-700); spot LPG premiums of $200-300; US LPG cargoes carry high freight (~90-day round trip).

subsections.label: Currency
points: Sharp INR depreciation could affect foreign component of projects, though impact limited given fixed-price awarded contracts and small foreign components.

subsections.label: Capex outlook
points: FY27 capex target INR25,000 crores, may cross to INR26,000-27,000 crores by year-end if things go smoothly. Allocation: refinery + petrochemicals ~INR11,000 crores (Bina, polypropylene at Kochi, PRFCC at Mumbai plus regular refinery capex); marketing/retail/infrastructure/supply logistics ~INR10,000 crores; BPRL equity infusion ~INR2,250 crores; CGD network ~INR1,700 crores.
Capital allocation approach remains prudent and disciplined with continued focus on project execution, balance sheet strength and sustainable returns.
No review of existing announced projects; assuming normalization after some point.

subsections.label: Balance sheet / debt outlook
points: Not foreseeing any big jump in debt equity provided crude prices settle; hopeful price stability and normality by July-August once war and Strait of Hormuz blockade are removed.
Long-term debt to equity not expected beyond 1:1 at group peak level; to return to 0.4-0.5 after project commissioning.

subsections.label: Refining margin guidance
points: Company generally avoids giving guidance on indicative GRMs as many parameters influence it; cannot give guidance on inventory gains.

themes.label: Geopolitical uncertainty
themes.note: West Asia tension and Strait of Hormuz disruption drove crude/product price volatility, term-supply shortfalls and a challenging Q1 FY27 outlook.

themes.label: Inventory management
themes.note: Crude at 27 days and products at 24 days; inventory gains helped Q4 refining margins amid price fluctuations.

themes.label: Capex cycle
themes.note: FY27 capex target raised to INR25,000 crores (possibly INR26,000-27,000 crores) across Bina, Kochi PP, PRFCC Mumbai, marketing, BPRL and CGD.

themes.label: Market discipline
themes.note: Severe under-recoveries with no price-recovery roadmap; management can absorb only 1-2 months of cash-flow mismatch and targets 32% retail share long-term.

themes.label: Crude sourcing diversification
themes.note: Russian crude raised to ~40-41% with 8 new grades across 4 regions; spot now 55-60% versus 45% planned.

themes.label: Renewable energy investment
themes.note: 251 MW installed plus 100 MW under execution; 2 GW target, output used within refineries despite lower 8-9% returns.

themes.label: Upstream project execution
themes.note: Mozambique force majeure resolved (first LNG mid-2028); Brazil FID approved but delayed to 2031-32 with INR4,300 crore impairment.

key_takeaways: We have increased our Russian crude procurement from 25% in Q3 to 31% in Q4, and it continues to increase fill up our supply gaps in the light of the current situation. Further, we have diversified to 8 new grades of crude during the year, covering 4 geographical regions. I would also like to assure stakeholders that crude supplies have been secured through July 2026.

During the year, our refineries operated at 116% of utilization with refinery throughput of 41.15 MMT, which is highest ever and distillate yield of 84.54%, reflecting the strength and complexity of our refining portfolio. Our gross refining margin for the year 2025-'26 stood at USD11.74 per barrel.
During the year, our overall domestic sales volume stood at 54.18 million metric tons at an overall growth of 3.5%, with petrol sales growing by 5.7% and diesel by 1% and ATF is 11.4%.
BPCL commissioned 1,691 new retail outlets during this year, taking the overall retail network to 25,323 outlets.
On an overall basis, we incurred a capex of INR20,400 crores. The capex target for FY '26-'27 is INR25,000 crores.

The revenue from operations stood at INR134,896 crores. The stand-alone profit after tax at INR3,191 crores and the consolidated profit after tax was INR5,625 crores. Our stand-alone net worth as on 31st March 2026 is INR95,233 crore. The earnings per share for the quarter is INR7.47 per share.
While our financials for FY '25-'26 have been strong since the large impact of the war is not fully realized in Q4 due to timing differences. Q1 '26-'27 is going to be a challenging period.
pressing_questions: Is it fair to say there has been some inventory positive impact in the refining numbers for this quarter given the timing difference between stocks used and price behaviour?
What kind of supply sources are now tied up till July other than Russia, and will reliance on WTI/Venezuela impact distillate yield if Gulf crudes reduce further?
Why did you take an impairment even after construction restarted in Mozambique, and can you break up the INR4,100 crore BPRL carrying value across key assets?
Given a year of relative market share loss versus peers, what is BPCL doing over the medium term to reverse it?

Is there any relook at capex programs or the debt-to-equity trajectory given the operating cash-flow challenge, and is there any thought among OMCs to switch back to a regulated regime to recover under-recoveries?
What is the current delivered crude cost / premium over dated Brent including freight and insurance?
Could we see meaningful periodic price hikes rather than a complete move back to daily price revisions?

How is BPCL optimizing its capital structure to balance growth investments in refining, marketing and renewables with debt sustainability, and how will treasury strengthen liquidity, forex risk mitigation and funding diversification?
Given severe under-recoveries, what is the inflection point at which fuel prices are aligned to market and why can't OMCs return to the pre-2022 daily pricing mechanism?

quarters.summary: Pine Labs delivered ~20% YoY revenue growth in Q1 FY2027 (guided FY27 range of 21-23.5%, with Q1 expected at the lower end), with adjusted EBITDA pressured by front-loaded proactive investments in 500 sales people, telecom/network infrastructure, and cloud/AI capabilities; management expects contribution margin to return to the 73-74% range in H2, does not see EBITDA margin going below last year's 23.5%, and reiterates full-year working capital under 15% and ~29-30% full-year tax rate.

subsections.label: Overall financial performance
points: Management characterized Q1 as another very strong, powerful performance with ~20% YoY growth, versus full-year guidance of 21-23.5% growth, having earlier said Q1 would be at the lower end.
PBT was described as 'quite interesting' at ~Rs.38 Crores; PAT came in close to Rs.20 Crores.
Effective tax rate for the quarter was 46% because tax losses in individual international loss-making entities cannot be absorbed / are not recognized; full-year expected around 29-30%.
India continues to be taxed at 25.1%.

subsections.label: Front-loaded investments impacting EBITDA
points: Adjusted EBITDA came in at ~Rs.126 Crores versus a preferred ~Rs.135-140 Crores; management framed the gap as ~Rs.14 Crores, noting no pricing pressure or adverse market dynamics — these are proactive investments.
Cloud costs rose ~Rs.10-12 Crores on a quarterly basis; ~25-30% expected to recur, the rest treated as one-time.
Company signed a new multi-year contract with one of the leading global cloud providers, giving comfort on pricing so some of these costs should not return.
Cloud costs were previously guided to grow ~6% YoY.

Network costs rose ~Rs.10 Crores; this hits the contribution margin line (not below it); ~50% expected to continue on a recurring basis, driven by petroleum segment deployment (expanded to ~100,000 POS machines) requiring network upgrade and SIM upgrade, plus network upgrades in global markets.

subsections.label: Operating cash flow & working capital
points: Operating cash flow/working capital came in at ~16%; guidance is to keep it under 15% on a full-year basis, with variance across quarters.
Q1 is typically when large payouts happen — employee payments, variable pays, certain capex advances due to supply chain — yet still landed at ~16%.
FY26 demonstrated a tight working capital of ~13% to 15%.
On early settlement (ICB), there is cyclicality because Q1 ramps up after collection intensity in Q3 into Q4; contribution-related changes should not alter the working capital cycle.

subsections.label: Contribution margin economics
points: Management noted no other company at ~72%, 73%, 75% contribution margins, and intends to remain in that range.

Depreciation on terminals has been kept flat over the last six quarters while the business grew, by asking merchants to make upfront payments and buy terminals so inventory stays off Pine Labs' books.

This upfront-payment model solves both the depreciation problem and the merchant attrition problem (merchants who invest early do not switch midway), but brings low-margin revenue into the stream that dilutes contribution margin.

subsections.label: Issuing & Acquiring Platform (IAP)
points: International IAP grew 40%+ while overall growth was 21%; India IAP grew 24%.

Contribution margin in IAP declined because distribution (lower margin, ~30-40% CM) is growing faster than processing (near 100% CM), especially in international markets where distribution is the entry strategy before moving up to processing.
IAP take rate held at a healthy 1.3%; changes in headline take rates are arithmetic, driven by business mix.
In international markets distribution is used as an entry strategy (e.g., Amazon in Singapore for distribution, a large US restaurant chain moving from distribution to full processing).

Product stack is broader than gift cards: gift cards (e.g., a Nykaa gift card for client engagement/working capital), prepaid cards (forex prepaid, general purpose Visa/Master/Rupay prepaid), and credit issuing/acquiring.
Credit processing business (issuing + acquiring) is present in ~20 countries and is now ~Rs.100 Crores of revenue on a full-year basis.
Added ~10 new brands/logos in Q1; if a new gift card program launches in the market, there is an 85-90% chance Pine Labs drives it.

New India segments being pursued: gaming (e.g., Roblox in-app purchases via gift cards), employee benefits, meal card and fuel/expense card (launch by October for tax savings), and direct-to-consumer open-loop prepaid (Bharat Yatra NCMC metro cards ~15,000/month).

Distribution via own platform (Woohoo / Gift Card Marketplace), direct corporate tie-ups, and large marketplaces (CRED, Amazon); listing fees are part of direct cost. Brands now also listed on Zepto and Blinkit for gift card ordering.
EBITDA margin in the IAP/distribution+processing business continues to expand YoY.
Every incremental processing and distribution comes straight to the bottom line below the contribution line, funding long-term growth.
YoY increase in issuing revenues was Rs.56 Crores with a Rs.11 Crores increase in issuing segment contribution, an incremental contribution margin of ~20% in the issuing segment.

subsections.label: DITP (Digital Infrastructure & Transaction Platform)
points: DITP GTV grew only 4% YoY on a full-year basis, largely due to the bill payments business (Setu), which is per-transaction (not ad-valorem) pricing, where one client moved some transactions in-house.
India DITP growth was ~20-25%; across online, flow-based income and issuing side, businesses grew ~20-25% at minimum.

DITP contribution margin declined from 84.4% (prior year Q1) to 81.7% due to a conscious strategic call to move devices off balance sheet — ~25-30% of deployments now have merchants buy the device upfront, bringing low-margin revenue in; also impacted by network capacity investments.
Absolute contribution margin was ~Rs.125 Crores this quarter versus ~Rs.130 Crores last quarter.

Outside India, Pine Labs does not deploy terminals itself (does not do 'DITP' in the terminal-investment sense) — acts as software/tech and processing provider; e.g., deployed 30,000 terminals with GCash in Philippines over 9 months on software and transaction processing basis only.

subsections.label: Affordability / Flow-based services
points: Affordability grew ~20% YoY at a revenue level despite electronics/mobile phone price-ups and supply chain disruptions in the quarter; management declined to share volume numbers.
Flow-based services help brands, banks and financial institutions acquire, convert and engage customers — spanning EMI, offers, and consumer communications at point of purchase.
Flow-based income and transactions continue to rise steadily; implied flow take rate ~28 bps driven by mix between UPI (growing faster) and affordability.
Affordability monetization comes from fees from all stakeholders (merchant, brand, consumer, terminal); no revenue earned when a consumer converts to EMI on their own banking app.
MDR / aggregator income flows into flow-based income and has been increasing; growth ~60-70% given base effect, driven by mid-market, online business and DCC volumes on Pine Labs rails.
Over the next two quarters, management plans to start disclosing more detail on other flow-based revenue streams reaching meaningful levels.
Flow-based income and issuing side have historically grown ~25%+ YoY.

subsections.label: Offline POS / terminal business
points: ~70%+ of all offline POS transactions are now on UPI, and rising; average UPI ticket size north of Rs.1,400, showing premiumization of payment.
Merchants increasingly want screen-based / big-screen devices for UPI, ordering and payment completion; Pine Labs partnering with invoicing and ordering software players.
Mid-market merchants increasingly ask for complex integrations where payments become part of their workflow — described as Pine Labs' sweet spot.
Terminal-side business has grown 12-15% YoY historically.
Credit card transactions growing 10-15% in the market; Apple Pay expected to enter before year-end, seen as positive as more diversified payment types strengthen Pine Labs' payment stack.

subsections.label: Online business & agentic payments
points: Online business (closely tied to agentic payments) is gaining traction amid online-space consolidation, with merchants seeking new partners.
New online go-lives: IRCTC, Lenskart.com (long-time offline client now online); already large transaction volumes for Zepto, Croma, Reliance Digital.
Online revenues have grown over 3-4 years; online and bill payments have historically grown 50%+ YoY.
Growth hub: a tech platform giving brands/large enterprises insights on store transactions and consumers; revenue becoming fairly interesting on a full-year basis.

subsections.label: AI initiatives
points: At least four divisions have 90% of all new code written using AI.
AI used aggressively in call center and back offices to drive efficiency.

First payments company in India to deliver an end-to-end agentic payment transaction — demonstrated at investor day with a buyer agent and seller agent communicating, using UPI mandate capabilities underneath.
Seeing great demand in the Indian market on the agentic payment side, flowing through the online business.
AI-based enhanced/trust services including self-healing terminals (~50% of terminals now self-healing), driving merchant stickiness and reducing field force and tag-to-recovery over time.

subsections.label: New products
points: SignalIQ: signed 6 banks and NBFCs; lets banks integrate their data and consumer data to find signals to underwrite consumers better — reflecting the thesis that payments plus data is the future.
Full tech stack on credit on UPI in place (NPCI promoting credit on UPI); J&K Bank has gone live with Pine Labs.
EMI product going global.
Growth hub tech platform for brand/enterprise insights.

Terminal management technology: a central infrastructure managing terminals from various providers on one platform, offered to banks and financial institutions; required pushing more data/capabilities onto the terminal network.
Integrating Play Store-related items so devices from different OEMs are integrated to a certain platform; the device is a platform for merchants to render AI-based solutions.
Instant inventory creation on the processing side at the moment a customer buys a product, so no card inventory flows through Pine Labs' books.

On the OMC contract, of the full-term expected value ($100 illustrative), ~60-70% captured, with more (~30-35%) to come in Q2 and Q3.

GCash (Philippines) — deployed 30,000 terminals in the last nine months on software and transaction processing basis (no terminal-side revenue).

points: Malaysia: now the single largest installment payments provider; working with ~8-9 banks (all except one large bank).
Replicated installment services in Singapore; about to launch in Dubai markets.
Five-person teams in Australia and the US; hired a sales leader for Singapore.
Signed the biggest organized restaurant chain in the US for processing services.
Signed British Airways for its entire gift card program to run on the Pine Labs stack (just signed, pending implementation).
Significant business in UAE/Dubai with two large customers; Q1 saw a dip in international transactions, described as not structural or long-term.

Mature markets like Malaysia project healthy EBITDA and contribution margin and are highly profitable; newer geographies (Singapore, Dubai) are in conscious-investment mode with early wins and large contracts underway.

subsections.label: Sales force investment
points: Invested in 500 new sales people over the last six months; full productivity typically comes 6-9-12 months after hiring — investment front-loaded.
The 500 are focused on India offline merchant/enterprise sales and online sales (D2C internet merchants seeking options).
Issuing/prepaid gift card sales team in India considered sufficient; global markets still being staffed (e.g., Singapore sales leader hired).

subsections.label: Competitive position & GTM
points: Wins essentially every deal on the street in India; ~90% full-stack market share driving brands to Pine Labs.
Large portion of growth comes from existing customers plus new brand/logo additions.
Merchants increasingly bringing digitization into stores and calling Pine Labs in.
Distribution and processing are seen as one value chain — distribution propels processing (and vice versa); brands like the instant inventory/tech model.

subsections.label: Vision & strategy
points: Reiterated vision to build a world-class fintech coming out of India / Asian markets.

Operates across the payments value chain: payments infrastructure/rails (online and offline, acceptance and issuing) — charging for payment acceptance, processing, and issuance/credit issuance — plus flow-based services around it.
Deliberate strategy not to use the balance sheet to drive revenues; avoids pre-purchasing brand inventory (which would resemble a lending business).
Offers to be a brand's distribution platform at a technology level even when distribution happens through another party (e.g., Gyftr), foregoing distribution margin but keeping tech platform usage.
Signed a new multi-year cloud contract with a leading global cloud provider.
Identified 2-3 new India IAP segments.

subsections.label: Management-flagged headwinds
points: Rising cloud costs globally after the AI rally; a portion (~25-30%) of the cloud cost increase expected to recur.
Recurring network cost increases (~50% of the increase) tied to petroleum-segment and international network/SIM upgrades.
International loss-making entities cannot absorb tax losses, pushing Q1 effective tax rate to 46%.
DITP GTV growth dropped to 4% due to a bill payments client moving transactions in-house.
Q1 international transaction dip (UAE/Dubai large customers), characterized as non-structural.
Electronics/mobile phone price-ups and supply chain disruptions during the quarter affecting affordability volumes.
Online-space consolidation (also framed as an opportunity as merchants seek new partners).

subsections.label: Forward outlook
points: Full-year revenue growth guided at 21-23.5%; comfortable with Q1 at ~20% (lower end); room to execute better toward a higher number.

Contribution margin expected to go higher in H2 and return to ~73-74% on a full-year basis, driven by (1) more processing on issuing side during festive season and (2) rising proportion of higher-margin flow-based revenues.
Management declined to give an EBITDA margin range but stated it will not go below last year's level (FY26 was 23.5%) without a doubt.
Full-year working capital to remain under 15% (variance across quarters).
Full-year effective tax rate comfortable at ~29-30%.
OMC contract: ~60-70% captured, ~30-35% more to come across Q2 and Q3.
Meal card and expense/fuel card to launch by October for tax savings.
Plan to start disclosing more detail on additional flow-based revenue streams over the next two quarters.
New markets (Singapore, Dubai) expected to reach breakeven over the next one to two years.
Incremental processing/distribution contribution will flow through at the same level as the existing stock over time.
Incremental CM flow-through to adjusted EBITDA expected at ~50-55%.

key_takeaways: Came in at about 20% on a year-on-year growth; guided to about 21-23.5% growth on a full year basis with Q1 generally on the lower end.

PAT came in close to Rs.20 Crores; PBT was about Rs.38 Crores; effective tax rate for the quarter was 46% because of unrecognized losses in international entities, with full-year comfortable at about 29-30%.

Adjusted EBITDA came in at ~Rs.126 Crores versus a preferred ~Rs.135-140 Crores, impacted by front-loaded proactive investments: ~Rs.10-12 Crores cloud/infra increase and ~Rs.10 Crores network cost increase; no pricing pressure or adverse market dynamics.
Invested in 500 new sales people over the last six months (full productivity in 6-9-12 months), front-loaded along with telecom/network and cloud capability investments.

Almost 70%+ of all offline POS transactions are on UPI, with average UPI ticket size north of Rs.1,400; DITP contribution margin moved from 84.4% to 81.7% on a conscious call to move devices off balance sheet.

Malaysia is now the single largest installment payments provider (working with ~8-9 banks); services replicated in Singapore and about to launch in Dubai; signed British Airways gift card program and the biggest US organized restaurant chain for processing.
First payments company in India to deliver an end-to-end agentic payment transaction; SignalIQ signed with 6 banks/NBFCs; J&K Bank live on credit on UPI; ~50% of terminals self-healing.
Full-year contribution margin expected to return to the 73-74% range in H2; EBITDA margin not to go below last year's 23.5%; working capital under 15% for the full year.

Have the OMC contracts started contributing fully to revenue, and how much scale-up remains?
What was the India GTV growth rate in DITP versus the reported 4% YoY?
For DITP contribution margin dropping from 84.4% to 81.7%, is it a mix shift toward mid-market given pricing power is said to be returning?
What are the levers to accelerate the domestic processing part of the IAP business?
Given significantly front-loaded investments this year, should the ~55% incremental CM flow-through be different this year?
Can you quantify the international entity losses this quarter and last full year, and when do they break even?

points: Came in with about 19% growth on the revenue side; H2 came in with almost 20% to 21% growth.
Adjusted EBITDA moved from around Rs.357 Crores to about Rs.559 Crores; almost 500 basis points improvement on EBITDA margin.
Delivered about Rs.113 Crores of PAT; management stressed strong conversion of revenue through contribution margin and adjusted EBITDA into PAT and PBT.
Started showing Rs.5 Crores to Rs.6 Crores of PBT positive in Q1/Q2 FY2026; management explained the business can run PBT positive and PAT positive for a long period.

subsections.label: Operating cash flow

On a full-year basis operating cash flow came in at about Rs.395 Crores; Q3 cash flows had turned negative earlier in the year.
Confident of significantly improving cash flow in FY2027.

subsections.label: Depreciation & amortization one-time item
points: A Rs.6 Crores QoQ D&A item: about Rs.4 Crores to Rs.5 Crores is a year-end clean-up of any obsolescence based on what can be collected from merchants — a one-time annual activity, not recurring.
Rest is linked to certain business growth seen with oil marketing companies; on a run-rate basis it will be lower.

subsections.label: Capex
points: Capex in operating cash flow of Rs.238 Crores; adjusted for certain opening payouts the run rate is about Rs.180 Crores to Rs.190 Crores.
Of Rs.238 Crores, about Rs.160 Crores to Rs.170 Crores pertains to DCPs, more or less on run rate; the rest relates to certain older payments.

Because of the chip shortage, suppliers asked for advances/100% advance while deliveries were pending, so CWIP got covered in the procurement; revenue could not be booked while advances were incurred.
Similar situation to the COVID period when the company upped inventory built in the business.

subsections.label: Contribution margin
points: Operating at world-class contribution margin levels (~75% range) vs Google at ~56% to 58%; company operates on a net revenue basis (no grossing up, takes net not 2%).
As newer business lines come in (e.g., employee benefits) the revenue mix could move contribution margin by 2% to 3% up or down; no intent to change the net-revenue operating model.

In the issuance business the value proposition is not just backend tech infrastructure but partnering with brands in acquiring/retaining customers and card distribution; distribution is additive to EBITDA even if smaller at contribution level and fuels the processing business.

Sameer: no margin pressure; in fact seeing some price-ups in some segments; whatever change seen is purely an outcome of business mix. Distribution is the only number at a gross revenue level due to accounting; everything else is 100% net revenue. Processing flow-through is almost 95% to 98%.
Contribution margin moved around in a 2% to 3% range across FY2026 quarters (Q2 slightly lower, Q3 higher, Q4 slightly lower).

subsections.label: Working capital and early settlement / bill discounting
points: Working capital typically in the range of 14% to 15% and remained in that range beyond early settlement; last year's Q3 peak of 22% was cyclical to festivity and normalized on a full-year basis.
Some receivables taken off balance sheet via factorization; serious drive on collections efficiencies contributed to working-capital efficiency beyond early settlement.
Bill discounting is a program (not a one-time activity) requiring collaboration/documentation with banks and brands; it will not remove all ICB balances but has been accelerated.

Flow business take rate of 30 bps is an aggregation of multiple revenue line items (affordability, UPI, DCC etc.), not just affordability; affordability take rates remain strong; take rate as a mix changes (e.g., higher UPI volumes lower the blended take rate).
No change in accounting from the bill discounting; the source of financing can change; affordability revenue recognition unchanged; balance-sheet impact from factorization only.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Rs.2700 Crores of cash plus organic free cash flow generation; healthily capitalized for all growth initiatives; no interest in raising funds.

ESOPs issued at or near FMV (three-month market rate driven, close to market price); very small deep-discount ESOPs may exist but are minimal. All FY2026 ESOPs issued at or near FMV, not at deep discount.

subsections.label: Business structure
points: Two large business lines: (1) digital infrastructure and transactions business, and (2) issuing and acquiring side (now almost ~30% of revenues).

Within digital infrastructure and transactions there are three parts: offline and online infrastructure business (operating with large merchants); flow-related transaction services monetized by transaction or value of flow; and Fintech infrastructure for banks/financial institutions and merchants.

Layered model: bottom layer is infrastructure and its distribution (~2 million touch points); middle delivers sector-specific solutions for retailers and banks; third layer brings customers via affordability, loyalty, rewards, cashbacks; newest is data-based monetization / marketing services.

subsections.label: Offline and online infrastructure
points: Present with the top three e-commerce companies and top three quick-commerce companies via payment-gateway-based platform; online business grew almost 60% YoY and is seen as a significant growth area.
Complex loyalty solution developed for the petroleum sector announced with three petroleum companies.
Sub-enterprise merchants (five/six stores) infrastructure business grew almost 30% YoY with about 7% improvement in unit economics.
In select segments, ~7% improvement in unit economics over the last six months.

subsections.label: Flow-based / affordability business
points: Continue to gain market share in affordability; increased the number of brands and signing up more NBFCs to deliver credit at point of purchase (no own NBFC — merchants do not want Pine Labs wedded to one NBFC).
More NBFCs = more lines of credit and more brands where subvention is possible — a strong network play.

Some large banks pulling back subvention offers as certain categories mature (e.g., a large bank reduced offers with a large mobile phone brand over 2-3 years); banks promoting affordability in new areas such as EVs and non-consumer-durable brands.

Where consumer durables uptake is lower, affordability uptake dips; company competes against new lines of credit (e.g., a world-class NBFC delivering point-of-purchase credit for 10 years) by growing store count and credit lines delivered per store to maintain YoY growth.
Multiple flow-based revenue lines: DCC, consumer Fintech partnerships (at least three-four) delivering offers at point of purchase (e.g., 50% off coffee converted to offer-based transaction).

Affordability is broader than lending: post-purchase installment programs, classic personal loans, insurance, trade-in, early buybacks; company not yet playing in new-credit-at-point-of-purchase (PL / consumer durable loans) due to insufficient NBFC coverage.
Affordability done in both offline and online segments; larger online market including non-CDIT.
Non-electronics affordability grew 60% full year (about 40%-45% last quarter) but is less than 5% of the segment relative to electronics — an area to invest in.

subsections.label: Issuing & acquiring / gift cards / IAP
points: Issuing business showed tremendous growth in India and global markets; new use cases from wallets, rewards as an infrastructure play.
RBI streamlining processes/governance of the prepaid (PPI) business, which management appreciates.
Big opportunity in employee benefits — an employee benefits program to be launched over coming weeks/quarters addressing many consumers and corporates.

Distribution and processing are an integrated offering to brands (acquire, retain, grow customers, lifetime value), not two separate businesses; processing flow-through is 95%-98% (tech/AWS/people cost sits below contribution margin); distribution has no incremental cost beyond partner listing-fee shares.

Strong distribution and processing market share in India; international IAP business growing at 44%, started with processing for brands like Woolworths and certain airlines and now building distribution traction internationally.

subsections.label: Data / analytics monetization (SignalIQ)
points: Launched SignalIQ, which looks at consumer data within the account-aggregator framework and delivers analytics-based solutions for better underwriting on behalf of partners.
About eight clients either in pilot or fully contracted for SignalIQ.
Using AI on merchant/consumer data to create new revenue streams delivering consumer insights, a new revenue line growing over the last two years.

subsections.label: Monetization headroom (GDV vs revenue)
points: GDV growth ~50% vs revenue growth ~19%; management confirmed headroom to increase monetization by moving toward more value-based revenue.
Distribution layer is largely linear with nearly all revenues recurring; base layer is largely MSF (rentals); now monetizing GTV through multiple flow and affordability revenue cohorts.

subsections.label: OMC (petroleum) business
points: OMC / petroleum is one of Pine Labs' oldest businesses; deploying terminals at ~50,000 fuel pumps (~130,000 POS machines).
About 50% of the steady-state volume already captured; deployment changing on a monthly basis; actual device deployment higher than 50% while some transactions have not yet started.
50% market share in fuel retail outlets.

Multiple revenue lines from OMCs: forecourt controller integration/fuel pump automation; payment infrastructure deployment; transaction/flow-based revenues; loyalty services (e.g., Indian Oil 'extra power' loyalty card managed end-to-end for five years); and newer IOT-related tenders being bid for.
Indian Oil 'extra power' loyalty program is an L1 tender worth about Rs.60 Crores to Rs.65 Crores over a five-year period (nothing to do with terminals).

Fully ready infrastructure platform where a stable-coin-based account/wallet can have a Visa or Mastercard prepaid card delivered in global markets; e.g., a UAE bank wanting a stable-coin-backed prepaid card — Pine Labs built the entire backend, bank owns the business/consumer, Pine Labs paid per transaction.
Starting sales activities in the next month to get more clients on the stable-coin-backed prepaid platform; entirely in global markets, nothing to do with India.

subsections.label: Competitive pullback
points: Competition backing off segments because their requirements/business models differ; newcomers pulling out of far-flung OMC / highway / village locations as it is not economically viable without an offline presence.

Some players focus on financial-services monetization (lending) rather than payment-based revenues, so target a different merchant base — an OMC does not need a loan; Pine Labs does no lending business and focuses on merchants who pay for its technology (its 'bread and butter').

Banks and FIs increasingly realize payments is a unique proposition and are calling Pine Labs more; direct-to-merchant strategy paying off; Pine Labs increasingly visible in metros at restaurants, petrol pumps and multi-store merchants.

subsections.label: Long-term stickiness
points: Payments infra business is long-term infrastructure partnerships; for a bank/retailer to replace or displace Pine Labs is a nine-month effort, giving ~nine months' visibility on revenue and low risk of a large revenue miss.

key_takeaways: We came in with about 19% growth on the revenue side. On an adjusted EBITDA side, from somewhere around Rs.357 Crores of adjusted EBITDA, we have now delivered about Rs.559 Crores on adjusted EBITDA. We made almost about 500 basis points improvement on the EBITDA margin side.

Going into FY2027, we have not really given a very specific guidance in terms of EBITDA, but what we have done is we have given out a hard guidance when it comes to revenues. We think we will be able to grow at about 21% to 23.5% on a year-on-year basis as far as revenue is concerned.

We delivered about Rs.113 Crores as far as PAT is concerned. I am glad to say that we delivered almost about Rs.676 Crores of cash flow in Q4 only... on a full year basis where we came in at about Rs.395 Crores of operating cash flow.
On a full year basis, we came in almost close to about $200 billion of payment volume... we are at about 2 million touch points today in the field.

In the online space... we have actually now grown that business almost by 60% on a year-on-year basis. All the three quick-commerce companies, all the three e-commerce companies are today using Pine Labs as a platform.
In our business, almost 89% of all new code, which has been written within Pine Labs over the last two quarters has been completely AI generated.
As far as the issuing business is concerned, our issuing business has shown tremendous growth not just in India but also in global markets... it is now almost about 30% of our revenues.
We have Rs.2700 Crores of cash. We also are organically generating free cash flows... we are quite healthily capitalized for all the growth initiatives we have in mind.

subsections.label: Macro backdrop
points: Equity indices staged a broad-based recovery over the quarter, navigating geopolitical uncertainty with resilience.
This resilience was equally visible in flows into the domestic asset and wealth management ecosystem, reaffirming conviction in the industry's structural growth story.
India's wealth market remains deeply underpenetrated and represents a significant growth opportunity; for a franchise positioned at the premium end, this is an opportunity to compound leadership.

subsections.label: Net flows commentary
points: Net flows of ~40,000 crores represent 12-15% of the opening ARR AUM base of ~2,40,000 crores.
Net flow split expected to be broadly 70:30 or 75:25 in favour of wealth business.

Asset management net flows were lopsided/negative in the quarter due to one large institutional mandate reducing allocation from ~$550-600 million to ~$175-180 million; broader FII/global allocations to listed equity have been muted over last 6-9 months, though alternates flows have been strong.
Multiple product launches planned over next 6-9 months expected to average out flows between wealth and asset management.
PMS as a structure is challenged structurally versus AIF, mutual fund or SIF vehicles for the same product; strategy remains alive but flows likely to migrate to pooled structures.

subsections.label: Cost-to-income drivers
points: HNI business AUM grew from ~600 crores to ~3,900-4,000 crores last year, and further to ~5,100-5,200 crores this quarter; platform stable, execution digital, run with 65-70 people.
A small set of clients (2-10 crore segment) to be migrated into HNI piece over next 2-3 months.
HNI business expected to not only break even but move into slight profitability this year.
ET Money run-rate loss (excl. exit-related costs) is now ~3-3.5-4 crores per quarter, down from 7 crores last quarter, expected ~6-7 crores this quarter, trending toward breakeven by Q4.
ET Money and HNI improvements expected to reduce cost-to-income by ~100-150 bps combined.
Operating leverage from alternates and wealth management businesses expected to take cost-to-income from 51% to ~49-49.5% by Q4, and ~100-150 bps improvement for the full year.
Core stable UHNI cost-to-income typically ~45%, with 100-200 bps buffer for expansion/new hires; long-term convergence expected toward 44-45% to 46-47% zip code depending on recruitment pace.

Variable vs permanent cost nature: hiring/team costs tied to GBs/JBs (guaranteed/joining bonuses) take 24-30 months cycle (vs 12-18 months) to normalize as new hires rebuild their book; industry equilibrium has not changed dramatically over last 2-3 years.

subsections.label: Retention/yield drivers
points: Retention decline attributed roughly half to carry recognition (largely asset management side, partially wealth) and half to business mix (advisory vs distribution mix, and typically lower TBR in Q1-Q2 vs Q3-Q4).
No reduction in margins seen within any specific business line; decline is purely a mix effect.
Only area of expected continuing headline retention pressure is the pure listed side of asset management business (8-9% of revenue).
AIF-only carry yield estimated at ~4 bps (range 3-5 bps) on ~58,000-60,000 crores alternates AUM, implying ~240 crores annual carry revenue.

subsections.label: Exceptional costs
points: ~12-13 crores exceptional cost this quarter relates to ESOPs tied to the B&K acquisition, not a recurring/constant item.

subsections.label: New SAR grant
points: New SARs (~12 lakh) announced; cost will start accruing only from next quarter once approved and allotted, spread over 4 years (~60 crores total notional impact of ~130-140 crores value).

subsections.label: HNI business
points: HNI proposition scaling well as a natural extension of the UHNI franchise.
Program supported by digital-first, scalable operating model, state-of-the-art client and RM app, and referrals from existing client and RM base.
Expected to break even on direct cost by end of this year as business momentum and productivity build through the year.
Revenue recognition of assets moved to HNI starts with a 12-month lag; trail revenue for assets moved a year ago has just started accruing.
HNI retention will be higher than UHNI distribution retention once mature (85-90 bps vs 71-73 bps for UHNI distribution).

subsections.label: ET Money
points: FY26 was a year of deliberate strategic transformation of ET Money, resetting the business model towards profitability.
Expect business to reach breakeven this year.

subsections.label: Institutional business / B&K integration
points: Institutional equity franchise continues to perform strongly.

Synergies envisaged at acquisition are coming to life: broking income from UHNI clients seeing uplift, and access to 600+ corporate treasuries opening cross-sell into wealth, treasury advisory and lending.

ECM-focused IB capabilities still building out but showing strong early traction; broking mix expected to turn steadily more annuity-like as institutional business scales and UHNI participation rises.

Biggest synergy in immediate short term is on equity brokerage side: combined B&K + UHNI brokerage grown from ~250-260 crores at deal close to ~310-320 crores currently, expected to grow at healthy clip of 15-20% per year for next 2-3 years.
Integration of B&K research into HNW fold expected to make equity brokerage one of the fastest-growing TBR line items.

subsections.label: Asset management business
points: Continues to be a structural growth engine; AUM crossed key milestone of Rs 1 lakh crore.
Strong momentum across alternates platform: private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, renewables, multi-asset, plus listed strategies.
Product engine remains active; continuing to broaden shelf across AIF, PMS, MF platforms including SIFs.

subsections.label: UHNI wallet-share dynamics
points: Number of clients with AUM >Rs 10 crore grown from ~1,800-2,000 (36 months ago) to just above 4,000 currently; these clients typically have only 15-20% wallet share with the firm today.
Growing this base from 4,000-5,000 to 6,000-8,000 clients seen as key to AUM growth via wallet share expansion.
Most clients deal with two or two-and-a-half advisors; ability to be part of that core two (rather than one of four/five) is a key differentiator.
Clients above Rs 250 crores are 70-80% on advisory side; Rs 50-250 crore (or 100-250 crore) segment is roughly 50-50; Rs 10-50 crore segment more skewed toward distribution.

Advisory mix on UHNI incremental flows expected to be ~60-40 advisory-led; advisory clients use the platform ~3x more (trusts, Gift City investments, borrowing, equity brokerage) than distribution clients, so overall retention between advisory and distribution clients is not dramatically different despite lower headline advisory retention.

subsections.label: ECM business build-out
points: Team of 6 people added: 4 on coverage side plus 2 strategic hires on process/compliance side; some serving notice period, some already joined.
Full-strength ECM team expected by October-December, with active pitching for mandates likely from January next year.
Currently a very small business benefiting from existing distribution strength and promoter connects rather than dedicated ECM origination.

subsections.label: Transaction Brokerage Revenue (TBR) composition
points: Large lumpy transactions (e.g., fixed income, private equity syndications) becoming less frequent as co-investment regulation and AIF-PMS vehicles allow long-term money collection for single instruments, converting transaction brokerage income into ARR assets over time.
Only one large lumpy transaction seen in Q4 last year; going forward, ability to have individually large TBR transactions is declining.

Efforts made to keep TBR consistent at Rs 125-150 crores range, targeting modest 10-15% growth over next 2-3 years; overall composition includes equity brokerage (listed), fixed income brokerage, unlisted equity brokerage, real estate/insurance brokerage, and merchant banking income.

TBR expected to stay below 25% of overall revenue mix, but proportion should rise from 15-20% toward ~20% as ARR AUM grows faster than TBR revenue in absolute terms; targeting overall organic growth of 15-20% a year in this bucket.

subsections.label: UHNI franchise strategy
points: UHNI franchise remains an anchor of the firm and continues to perform very well.
Focus consistent across three vectors: deepening wallet share of existing clients, extending beyond top cities, and being manager of first-choice post-monetization events.
Advisory-led proposition gaining traction as clients migrate from transactional, product-driven engagement to portfolio-level, solution-oriented mandates.
Continued investment ahead of the curve across RM capabilities, technology, portfolio analytics, and client data security.

RM target of 350-400 senior RMs over medium term against 9,000-10,000 family target (vs 4,100 today, addressable market of 40,000-45,000 UHNI households); requires ~30-40 RM additions per year over next three years (~300-350 total RMs to service 10,000 families), with internal junior RMs also escalating to senior roles.

subsections.label: UBS collaboration
points: Steady progress across various components of the UBS collaboration; cross-referral programs across NRI, resident, and global mandates showing early traction, expected to convert into meaningful flows over the medium term.
UBS's global distribution expected to open up offshore capital access for alternates and listed strategies during this year.
Onboarding of funds mutually and client referrals began January-March of current year; expect funds launched both ways (UBS launching 360 ONE funds and vice versa) in the coming quarter.
Conservative AUM exchange target of $500-600 million between the two organizations over time, used as the measure of collaboration success rather than immediate cost-to-income/profitability impact.

Both organizations seen as mutually accretive at whatever retention is agreed; exact unit economics/retention terms still to be discovered over next six months as market develops.

subsections.label: Leadership continuity
points: CEO addressed market murmurs about his continuation post any Bain investor step-back; clarified his tenure as CEO is unrelated to his equity shareholding.

Continuation as CEO depends on personal desire/passion (unchanged after 25 years in the business), health (currently 49 years old), and continued alignment of interests; management and CEO remain 85-100% mentally/emotionally invested and >90% financially invested in the business.
No defined timeline (3/5/7/10 years) — approach is continuous, with no factors currently pointing to a change.
CEO noted he has answered the succession question 125 times over 18 years.

key_takeaways: Our total ARR AUM increased by 19% to Rs 3,42,000 crores, with wealth AUM at Rs 2,42,000 crores, a growth of 24.2%, and asset management AUM at Rs 1,00,000 crores, an increase of 8.2%. Overall, AUM rose by 17% to Rs 7.8 lakh crores as on June 30, 2026.

We garnered the ARR net flows of Rs 10,815 crores in this quarter as compared to Rs 8,985 crores in the previous quarter. The wealth business drove the increase contributing strong flows of Rs 13,379 crores as compared to Rs 6,957 crores in Q4.
On the asset management side, even as gross flows remained very strong at approximately Rs 4,000 crores, the net flows were negative due to one large outflow in an institutional mandate.

Q1 FY27 ARR revenues stood at Rs 614 crores, up 20.3% year on year, with ARR revenue now comprising 75% of total revenue from operations. ARR retention was at 74 basis points, with wealth at 71 and asset management at 83 basis points. TBR rose by 37.3% year on year to Rs 208 crores during the quarter. Total revenue increased 20% to Rs 870 crores driven by strong growth across both wealth and asset verticals.

Total cost stood at Rs 446 crores with a cost to income ratio of 51.3% as compared to 53.5% in Q4 FY26. We expect gradual improvement in this metric as the businesses scale up, we drive synergies from strategic initiatives and incoming wealth teams reach full productivity.

We are very happy to report a profit after tax of Rs 330 crores an increase of 14.8%. Tangible ROE stood at 19.4% and we expect this to improve as capital deployed in our lending and asset businesses begin to reflect in earnings.
The program now spans approximately 60+ relationship managers across 12 locations, managing in excess of Rs 5,000 crores of AUM for 800+ clients at ARR retention yield of around 90 basis points.

As business momentum continues and productivity builds through the year, we expect the [HNI] business to break even on direct cost by end of this year. FY26 was a year of deliberate strategic transformation of the ET money business, resetting the business model towards profitability. We expect the business to reach break-even level this year.

AUM has now crossed key milestone of Rs 1 lakh crore with strong momentum across our alternates platform, comprising of private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, renewables, and multi-asset, as well as listed strategies.
pressing_questions: First question is basically on the net flows. I think, you know, we are on the target to achieve that '12 to 15% of opening net flows, but do you think it will be more lopsided towards wealth as AMC is kind of, you know, seeing outflows, specifically in the PMS over the last two to three quarters?

My second question is on the cost-to-income ratio. I think we have this kind of mandate to, you know, go at least 150-200 basis point decline, but this quarter also, it was more than 51%. So, should we expect the remainder of FY27 to have that operating leverage and declining cost-to-income?

An industry question, wherein, you know, we are a significant player in the private credit industry. So just wanted to know, you know, how do you see the future for this segment and how are we kind of positioned to, you know, increase our dominant position further?

Karan, if you can delve some bit on the unit economics of the [UBS] business that you would have in mind, if you kind of reach the $500-600 million asset transfer between the two entities, what kind of revenue potential, or does it operate at a similar cost structure of what we have today?

Over the last couple of months, there have been a lot of murmurs about, you know, when Bain as an investor steps back, you as the CEO might also take a backseat... if you won't mind sharing what, how you think yourself at, from a 3 to 5-year perspective, running 360 ONE, a lot of us would love to hear your thoughts around it.

quarters.summary: Management framed FY26 as a "landmark year" with strong ARR AUM/revenue growth, record PAT, and platform expansion (B&K/360 ONE Capital integration, ET Money, UBS collaboration, HNI Reserve program). For FY27 and beyond, management guided to 12-15% opening AUM net flow growth in Wealth, AUM growth of 20-25%, RM addition of 25-30% per year, and profit growth of 15-25% on the Wealth Management side, while targeting cost-to-income reduction to 45-48% over 2-3 years and quarterly TBR run-rate of ~175-200 crores versus prior guidance of 125-130 crores. ET Money is expected to head toward breakeven in the near term, and the Investment Banking platform under 360 ONE Capital is expected to begin meaningful contribution over the next 12-18 months.

subsections.label: P&L Drivers
points: FY26 was a landmark year with strong financial outcomes and meaningful platform expansion to complete the flywheel.
Q4 revenue growth of 18.5% was driven by strong growth across both Wealth and Asset verticals, partially offset by lower other income.

Q4 Transaction and Broking revenue strength partly reflects full quarter consolidation of 360 ONE Capital (formerly B&K Securities), whose broking revenue adds a structurally more consistent annuity-like component to a historically more transactional revenue stream.
FY26 costs not directly comparable to FY25 due to consolidation of B&K Securities and ET Money.

Higher blended cost-to-income ratio reflects investment phase of newer businesses (HNI Reserve, ET Money, 360 ONE Capital); gradual improvement expected as these businesses scale and reach full productivity via synergies and incoming Wealth team productivity.

subsections.label: Tax Matter
points: Received an order from tax authorities today (call date) with an aggregate demand of Rs. 336 crores.
Company believes it has duly discharged all tax liabilities as applicable and has adequate factual and legal grounds to substantiate its position.
Does not expect any material impact on financials or operations; will pursue appeals against the entire order under applicable laws.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation
points: Board approved first interim dividend of Rs. 6 per share, continuing disciplined capital allocation philosophy — returning surplus capital to shareholders while retaining capacity to fund growth in Lending, Alternates, and strategic initiatives.
Tangible ROE expected to improve as capital deployed in Lending and Alternate businesses begins to reflect in earnings.

subsections.label: Lending Book Quality
points: No margin funding (MTF) book to speak of — broker does not do MTF; book is less than Rs 50-60 crores.
Lending book is largely loan-against-shares, collateralized at 2x typically on a diversified portfolio; no stress observed despite market volatility.
Since 2016, the Lending business has been run without a single rupee of NPA or loss, focused on Lombard/portfolio lending to Wealth Management clients.

subsections.label: HNI Segment (Reserve Program)
points: Natural extension of the UHNI franchise and a powerful feeder pipeline into the core proposition.
With increased business momentum and productivity in the coming year, overall financial performance of this segment expected to improve significantly.
Revenue impact is muted because a large portion of assets are mutual funds and the broker code change affects revenue only after 12 months, but quality and quantum of business have been strong.
Tech platform is a unique 'phygital' model set up to service clients between Rs 2-25 crores, as opposed to purely online clients.

subsections.label: ET Money
points: FY26 was a year of strategic transformation on the business model and disciplined execution driving multiple on-ground changes.
Expected to head towards breakeven in the near term.

subsections.label: 360 ONE Capital (formerly B&K Securities)
points: Integration of B&K is now complete; Institutional Equities business rebranded as 360 ONE Capital.
Strategic synergies coming to life — brokerage revenues from UHNI clients seeing an uplift, and access to 600+ corporate treasuries opening distribution and lending channels.
Investment Banking platform is being built out and expected to begin meaningful contribution over the next 12-18 months.

B&K numbers steady for the last 10 months vs prior year, driven by early integration on the corporate treasury platform (introduction of large Wealth Management corporate treasury clients) and slight market share gain on equity side.
Regulatory approvals for B&K Capital to become 360 ONE Capital, and common research integration, only completed in last 15-30 days — integration benefits expected to come through soon.

subsections.label: Discretionary PMS (AMC)
points: Growth has been softer than desired; supplemented partly by growth on advisory side.
Strategy was, in retrospect, too benchmark-hugging/relative-return to index rather than customized — custom-mandate clients have done extremely well and continued to add AUM.
Management has pivoted strategy, launching changes in first week of June; expects those numbers to move up.
Q4 discretionary PMS retention increase was due to profit share on a small base, not a structural trend; retentions remain within range on a yearly basis.

subsections.label: RM / Team Leader Structure
points: Improved ratio of senior leaders to relationship managers over time — minimum recruitment benchmark for UHNI business is 'partner equivalent' (6-8 years prior experience).
Quality improvement and quantity optimization both achieved versus 5 years back; span of control automatically adjusts with quality improvement.
Plan to move senior team leader count from 70-75 to 120-130, partner level from 110-120 to ~240, and total RM count from 180-190 to 330-340.

subsections.label: Client Quality Evolution
points: Client base has become broader and deeper — sophisticated family offices (300-350) able to cut larger cheques and act as platform partners rather than single product allocators.
Portfolio-based approach (vs product-based) is driving higher average ticket sizes — no more than 25% in a single product, no more than 15% with a single asset manager.

Greater diversity in client geography (beyond first 6-7 cities) and background — professionals/professional entrepreneurs, corporate lawyers, movie stars, sportspeople, doctors now represent 15-20% of client base vs 5-10% earlier.
Area needing more work: greater participation from domestic institutions and insurance companies, which have become key contributors to Alternative Investment Funds.

subsections.label: Distribution Assets Net Flow
points: Distribution assets negative net flow largely not a function of large redemptions — mainly attributable to mark-to-market impact reducing trail income versus last quarter.
Negative Q4 net flow of Rs 212 crores in Wealth distribution assets was primarily contributed by Corporate Treasuries, not UHNI.

subsections.label: UBS Collaboration
points: Cross-referral programs in the Wealth business across NRI, resident, and global mandates showing positive early traction; expected to convert to meaningful relations over the coming financial year.
On Asset Management side, early synergies emerging with UBS's global distribution, providing a pathway for Alternate and Listed strategies to access offshore capital.

Product collaboration (360 ONE product on UBS AMC platform and vice versa) has been slower than desired — not from lack of intent but due to regulatory approval processes both in GIFT and on UBS platform taking longer; expected to progress over the next quarter or so.

subsections.label: Investment Banking Build-out
points: Building out Banking business in a measured, no-hurry manner given it's a relationship/execution-driven services business requiring the best people.
12 senior investment professionals identified to hire; 4 of 12 already in place; team expected to be substantially more competitive over next 3-4 months.

subsections.label: 10,000 Families Strategy
points: Strategic vision to serve ~10,000 families across all three business lines — Wealth management, capital provision at different balance sheet stages via fund management, and capital markets journey via 360 ONE Capital as these families/businesses grow.

subsections.label: Industry Consolidation Outlook
points: Management believes the industry requires at least 3-4 more larger players given its size, but expects it to remain fairly consolidated over the next 3-4 years given 'size begets size' dynamics.
A tighter/more consolidated market is viewed as helping the company consolidate its position faster.

subsections.label: Macro/Market Volatility
points: FY26 was undeniably challenging for Indian equity markets; equity indices touched bullish levels in H1 but saw phases of correction and sectoral rotation through the year, testing investor conviction.
Foreign and other investors withdrew nearly $15-20 billion, well mitigated by strong domestic flows especially through the mutual fund industry.
Management believes headwinds are largely priced in and policy environment is supportive; markets present an attractive entry point for long-term investors.

subsections.label: Tax Matter
points: Received tax demand order of Rs 336 crores; company believes it has adequate grounds and does not expect material impact; will appeal.

subsections.label: Execution & Talent Risk
points: Biggest risk (and opportunity) identified is execution — need for continuous attention to detail, response times, and professionalized organization as headcount grows (1,800 employees).
Investing heavily in middle management leadership depth to professionalize organization from the top.
War for talent is ongoing; company positions compensation between 90th-110th percentile — beyond 110th percentile becomes harder even for the firm to justify/manage.
Attrition risk acknowledged in markets like Delhi and Bangalore, but company has attracted strong replacement talent; prepared for 2-4% attrition annually.
Discretionary PMS underperformance attributed to a relative-return/benchmark-hugging strategy design, now being revised.

subsections.label: Lending/Credit Risk
points: No stress observed in loan-against-shares lending book despite market volatility in Q4, unlike some brokers experiencing stress on MTF books; company has no meaningful MTF book.
Lending book collateralized at 2x on a diversified portfolio; zero NPA/loss track record since 2016.

subsections.label: Yield/Pricing Pressure
points: Some degree of pressure on yields acknowledged as a constant, but management not overly concerned; broadly in line with expectations.

B&K/360 ONE Capital transactional revenue faces yield compression risk from mutual fund company fee changes effective April 1, but management still comfortable with 175-200 crore quarterly TBR guidance range.

subsections.label: Overall Outlook
points: As the firm looks toward FY27 and beyond, management remains confident despite ongoing volatility, citing 18 years of navigating challenging cycles, a strong balance sheet, talented team, and culture.

India seen at an inflection point with strong macroeconomic foundations, supportive regulatory environment, and an addressable market for Wealth, Asset Management, Alternatives and Lending expanding at an unprecedented pace.

subsections.label: TBR Guidance Revision

175-200 crore range not 'cast in stone' but considered a reasonable improvement versus the prior 125-140 crore range.

Equity and equity-related income (excluding banking) expected to roughly double over next 3-4 years combining 360 ONE Capital equities growth with wealth management equities uptake.

themes.label: ARR flywheel growth
themes.note: ARR AUM up 26% YoY to Rs 3,11,940 crores and ARR revenue up 34.5% YoY, now 75% of total revenue from operations.

themes.label: Acquisition integration (B&K/360 ONE Capital)
themes.note: B&K integration complete and rebranded as 360 ONE Capital; synergies emerging in brokerage uplift and corporate treasury access, though integration benefits still ramping.

themes.label: New business scale-up (HNI, ET Money, Banking)
themes.note: HNI Reserve program and Investment Banking build-out progressing steadily; ET Money targeting breakeven; all still in investment phase weighing on cost-to-income.

themes.label: Cost-to-income discipline

themes.label: Transaction/Broking revenue guidance revision
themes.note: Quarterly TBR guidance raised from 125-130 crores to 175-200 crores driven by asset-class diversification and B&K/360 ONE Capital consolidation.

themes.label: UHNI market consolidation & RM talent war
themes.note: Management sees industry staying consolidated over 3-4 years and plans to scale RM count from 180-190 to 330-340, but war for talent and 2-4% attrition remain ongoing risks.

themes.label: UBS strategic collaboration
themes.note: Cross-referral traction positive but platform product integration delayed by regulatory approvals in GIFT and on UBS platform.

key_takeaways: FY26 has been a landmark year for 360 ONE, one in which we have delivered strong financial outcomes, and also meaningfully expanded the platform to complete our flywheel.
Total ARR AUM increased to 311,940 crores, up 26% year-on-year, with Wealth ARR AUM at 2,16,000 crores and Asset Management ARR AUM at 95,000 crores.
FY26 ARR revenue stood at 2,289 crores, up 34.5% year-over-year, and ARR revenue now comprising 75% of total revenue from operations.
We are happy to report the company recorded its highest full-year PAT in FY26 of Rs. 1,225 crores, an increase of 20.7%.
The Board has approved the first interim dividend of Rs. 6 per share.
The integration of B&K is now complete, and the Institutional Equities business has been rebranded as 360 ONE Capital.

On ET Money, FY26 has been a year of strategic transformation on the business model and disciplined execution to drive multiple on-ground changes. With different engines at play, we would expect the business to head towards breakeven in the near term.
As an update to our past communication on tax-related matters, we have received an order today from the tax authorities with an aggregate demand of Rs. 336 crores.

We would love to do better on the mutual fund side, whereas emphasize and ensure that we have our clear leadership position maintained, both on the Wealth Management side as well as on the Alternate side.
We've been blessed to be a large participant in the market and have a large percentage of market share, and we only hope to be able to double our market share over the next 3 to 5 years.
pressing_questions: On the discretionary PMS, growth has been slightly softer than desired — what is the strategy to get back, especially on that segment?

On the UBS bit — in terms of referrals, how has the traction been? Any initial data point? And also, your product on UBS's AMC platform, and then your AMC product on their platform, when can we expect some things on those lines?

On a quarter-on-quarter basis, net flows have come down while retail brokerage has remained more or less steady — is this attrition-led, clients pulling out money, or avoidance of deployment given the volatile situation?

On DPMS, there is a sharp rise in retentions on both Wealth and Asset Management sides — is this new money coming in at higher retentions or older, lower-priced AUM going out, and what is the out-pricing risk given competitive intensity, especially on the Asset Management side?
Some colour on distribution assets where net flow is negative — how much of that negative net flow is from UHNI given HNI would have net positive cash flows?
On the team leader RM count — the count has been broadly flat for the last 3 years despite intense competition; what explains this?

quarters.summary: Tata Capital reported healthy Q1 FY27 growth (AUM up 22% YoY consolidated, 28% ex-Motor Finance; PAT up 56% YoY) with improving asset quality and operating leverage, and management reiterated it is on track to meet FY28 guidance (ROA of 2.6%, cost-to-income of 33-34%, credit cost within guided corridor, Motor Finance ROA of 2%, and AUM growth guidance of 23-25% for FY27). Two key developments during the quarter were the proposed acquisition of gold-loan company Yogloans (entry into secured gold lending) and a USD 400 million oversubscribed international bond issuance strengthening the funding mix.

subsections.label: AI-driven operating leverage
points: AI initiatives delivering 98% digital onboarding and AI-led underwriting, 40% productivity gains in operations, and stronger collections outcomes.
Cost-to-income ratio improvement attributed to technology, data infrastructure and distribution investments now translating into structural efficiency gains.
Headcount growth remains well calibrated; incremental hiring focused on frontline sales and collections roles only.
Manpower addition last year was just under 5% of total workforce; largely added only in front-end sales and collections.
Operating expense YoY growth of 21% was driven mainly by change in the annual appraisal cycle; normalized growth would be ~16-17%.
ROA improvement expected via two-thirds from margin expansion and one-third from operating leverage improvement.

subsections.label: Asset quality / provisioning
points: PCR change of 30-40 bps quarter-to-quarter is purely a function of the ageing mix within Stage-3 assets (incremental provisioning as accounts age within Stage-3), not a change in TTC PD/LGD assumptions.

ECL grades (PD/LGD) refreshed quarterly using trailing data (e.g., Q1 calculation uses data through March); ECL calculation horizon is 5 to 7 years depending on product life cycle; LGD is historical-to-date.
Credit cost decline of 26% YoY primarily driven by continued improvement in unsecured Retail portfolio.
Bounce rates continue to improve month-on-month, including in the current month, per management.

subsections.label: Capital planning
points: Endeavor to operate capital adequacy/CET1 at least 200-250 bps above mandated regulatory thresholds.
Company well capitalized until June-September 2028 based on current book growth guidance.

subsections.label: Calendar day / margin impact
points: No impact from difference in number of days between Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 on margins/interest expense.

subsections.label: Book growth drivers
points: Disbursement growth outpacing AUM growth as book growth lags disbursement growth in early stages of any lending scale-up; expect gap to narrow over next 2-3 quarters.
Corporate and SME segments continuing to scale steadily; Corporate segment viewed as having largely maxed out its share, with more incremental growth expected from Retail and SME.
In each business line (Housing, Retail, SME, Corporate, Prime Home Loans) effort is to increase margins even outside the high-margin product mix shift.
If Corporate origination exceeds desired proportion, company will sell down/syndicate to keep Retail+SME within the 85-88% corridor.
Contribution of high-yield/unsecured products expected to make unsecured book grow faster than overall book by Q3/Q4 of this financial year.

No PLR (base rate) hikes taken on SME/Corporate book; strategy instead is to price incremental lending better to grow NIMs faster than cost-of-funds growth, applied across Housing, Retail, SME and Corporate.

subsections.label: Motor Finance transformation
points: Transformation journey progressing as planned with focus on a more balanced, sustainable portfolio; measured growth approach amid geopolitical uncertainty and elevated fuel costs led to sequential book decline.
Business became profitable from Q4 of last year and remained profitable in Q1 FY27 despite seasonal increase in credit cost.
Continuing to expand presence beyond captive OEMs while enhancing efficiency through branch and workforce rationalization.
Mix shift expected: proportion of ILMSCV to increase, proportion of HCV to reduce; combined with rate increases across segments to improve yields and margins.
Price gap between new and used vehicles has narrowed after GST rate rationalization.

subsections.label: Microfinance strategy
points: Model is JLG (Joint Liability Group), forming 99.9% of that business; right-to-win seen as operational excellence — correct KYC, income-source evaluation, timely digital collections, paperless processes.
Business seen as having room to scale, but management intends to keep it below 2% of total book for the foreseeable future.

subsections.label: Affordable/Micro Housing strategy
points: Affordable and Micro Housing chosen to target customers within a comfortable credit profile with low delinquency, leveraging cost-of-funds advantage for better ROA.
Micro Housing offers a better yield than Affordable Housing and will be grown faster.
